title: dev-team's expand_footprint() drops rename/move deletions when footprint uses glob patterns
details:
**What happened:** A `kind: chore` slice moved ~450 files from an old package path to a new one (directory rename via `mv`, not `git mv`). The plan.md footprint used glob entries for both the old and new path (e.g. `src/main/java/yama/game/mutantmerge/**` and `.../infinitystrikerampage/**`). `commit-work` succeeded and reported a commit, but `expand_footprint()` in devteam.py only resolves glob entries via `glob.glob()` against files that currently exist on disk — since the old directory no longer exists after the move, its glob matched nothing, so `git add -A -- <targets>` never staged the ~478 old-path deletions. They were left as unstaged `D` entries after the commit. `devteam next` then reported "NOT READY — uncommitted changes in <worktree>".
**What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model while orchestrating a dev-team run.
**Repro:** Plan a `chore`/`refactor` slice whose footprint is two glob patterns (old-path/**, new-path/**) for a directory that gets `mv`'d from old to new inside the slice. Run `commit-work`. `git status` afterward still shows the old path's files as unstaged deletions even though the commit succeeded.
**Evidence:** stable-be-infinity-strike-rampage repo, slice S1, commit 412a3cb46; `expand_footprint()`/`stage_footprint()` in ~/.claude/skills/dev-team-v3.2/scripts/devteam.py (around line 2649).
**Cause:** `expand_footprint`'s docstring says a path git already knows about is kept even if it no longer exists on disk, but that fallback only applies to literal (non-glob) footprint entries already present in the computed `paths` list — a glob entry that matches zero files on disk contributes zero candidate paths, so the "known to git" fallback never gets a chance to apply to the deleted files.
